```{r}
#| label: setup
source("R/metals.R")
library(ggplot2)
prices <- load_prices()
last_day <- max(prices$date)
fits <- lapply(stats::setNames(levels(prices$metal), levels(prices$metal)),
               function(m) forecast_metal(prices, m))
bt <- backtest(prices)
```

## What this is

- A small data product from the Coursera course *Developing Data Products* (2015),
  rebuilt in `r format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")` with Quarto.
- It downloads **five years** of daily prices of the four precious metals and
  forecasts the next **`r HORIZON` trading days** (about three months) with
  `auto.arima()` from the [forecast](https://pkg.robjhyndman.com/forecast/) package.
- It also checks the forecasts against a **naive** one (tomorrow = today), which
  is the honest benchmark for any asset price.
- Companion Shiny app: [Precious-Metals-Prediction](https://github.com/EnriquePH/Precious-Metals-Prediction).

::: {.aside}
Data up to `r format(last_day, "%d %B %Y")`. Not investment advice.
:::

## The data

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
| Metal     | Future | Exchange |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Gold      | `GC=F` | COMEX    |
| Silver    | `SI=F` | COMEX    |
| Platinum  | `PL=F` | NYMEX    |
| Palladium | `PA=F` | NYMEX    |

Daily settlement of the front-month future, in USD per troy ounce, from Yahoo
Finance; EUR and GBP prices use the `EURUSD=X` and `GBPUSD=X` rates of each day.
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| label: last-prices
last <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(prices, prices$metal), function(s) {
  s <- s[order(s$date), ]
  n <- nrow(s)
  year_ago <- s$usd[max(1, n - 252)]
  data.frame(Metal = s$metal[n], USD = s$usd[n], EUR = s$eur[n], GBP = s$gbp[n],
             `1 year` = sprintf("%+.0f %%", 100 * (s$usd[n] / year_ago - 1)),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(last, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = sprintf("Last price per troy ounce (%s)", format(last_day, "%d/%m/%Y")))
```
:::
:::

## Forecast: the next three months

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r}
#| label: forecasts
#| results: asis
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-width: 11
for (m in names(fits)) {
  cat("\n\n### ", m, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(plot_forecast(fits[[m]], m))
}
```

:::

::: {.aside}
ARIMA on the logarithm of the price, so the bands are never negative and widen
in proportion to the price. Dark band: 80 %; light band: 95 %.
:::

## Is ARIMA better than doing nothing?

```{r}
#| label: backtest
better <- sum(bt$`RMSE ARIMA` < bt$`RMSE naive`)
knitr::kable(bt, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Each model is fitted leaving out the last `r HORIZON` days and compared with
what really happened. ARIMA beats the naive forecast in **`r better` of 4**
metals. Prices behave almost like a random walk: the useful output is the
**width of the bands** (the risk), not the central line.

## The model, step by step

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
1. **Logarithm** of the price: changes become percentages.
2. **Differences**: `auto.arima()` tests for unit roots (KPSS) and almost always
   takes one difference, the daily return.
3. **Orders** *p* and *q* chosen by AICc.
4. **Residuals**: should look like white noise (Ljung–Box test, right).
:::

::: {.column}
```{r}
#| label: residuals
lb <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(m) {
  fit <- fits[[m]]$fit
  t <- stats::Box.test(stats::residuals(fit), lag = 20, type = "Ljung-Box",
                       fitdf = sum(fit$arma[1:2]))
  data.frame(Metal = m, Model = as.character(fit), AICc = fit$aicc,
             `Ljung-Box p` = t$p.value, check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(lb, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

A p-value above 0.05 means no autocorrelation is left in the residuals.
Volatility clusters (calm and stormy periods) remain: that is a job for GARCH
models, not ARIMA.
:::
:::

## Then and now

| | 2015 | `r format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")` |
|---|---|---|
| Slides | slidify (no longer maintained) | Quarto + reveal.js |
| Data | Oanda, last 180 days (service closed) | Yahoo Finance futures, 5 years |
| Charts | rCharts / Morris.js | ggplot2 + plotly |
| Evaluation | none | back-test against the naive forecast |
| Updates | by hand | GitHub Actions, every month |

The original slides are kept unchanged in
[`legacy/2015-slidify`](https://github.com/EnriquePH/Precious-Metals-Slidify/tree/master/legacy/2015-slidify)
(tag `slidify-2015`).
